title: Senior Director, Architecture & Quality – Connectivity Firmware
text:
**About Marvell**

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

**Your Team, Your Impact**

Marvell's Connectivity firmware organization delivers firmware for our connectivity and optics product lines. This role owns the full Architecture & Quality function for that portfolio. Architecture and quality operate as one integrated group, a shared resource to every firmware team and not a gate in front of them. 
 
You will set the technical architecture direction for the portfolio and hold the quality bar across it, treating the two as a single end-to-end responsibility. Architecture shapes what can be verified, and quality is how we prove it, from requirements through release and into the field. You will be accountable for how architecture decisions are made, how firmware is verified and released, and how well the firmware, hardware and systems teams work together. You will lead a global team of senior technical leaders and are expected to build depth in a function that is currently concentrated in a few people.

**What You Can Expect**

This is one function, not two. Architecture decisions set what can be tested, and quality findings feed straight back into architecture. You will own the full lifecycle from requirements and design through verification, release and field support.

**Architecture that is built to be verified**

* Product and systems architecture across the Connectivity firmware portfolio: reference architectures, standards, design reviews and technical decision records, each with testability and observability designed in.
* Product hardware interlink: the architectural contract between hardware and firmware, covering requirements, interface definition, bring-up readiness and silicon-to-firmware feedback loops, with validation criteria agreed up front.
* CMIS and optics architecture: firmware architecture for CMIS-based modules and optics products, including spec compliance, feature roadmap and interoperability, tied directly to conformance and interop test plans.
* Architecture governance that scales: lightweight review processes, clear ownership and reusable components, so teams move faster instead of waiting on reviews.

**Quality as an end-to-end discipline**

* Quality strategy that starts at requirements and architecture review, not at test execution: shift-left practices, requirements quality and design-for-test standards owned jointly with the architects.
* Software Quality Assurance (SQA) strategy and execution: test strategy, automation, regression coverage, release qualification and defect trends.
* Release readiness and quality gates for all firmware releases, with clear exit criteria and a straight, data-backed go/no-go recommendation.
* Quality metrics and reporting to Engineering leadership, Product Management and customer-facing teams.

**Closing the loop**

* Customer-escape and defect analysis that traces root causes back to architecture, interfaces and process, and turns the learning into updated patterns, standards and test coverage.
* A single set of metrics and quality signals shared across architecture, interlink, optics and SQA, so design risk and test findings are managed in one view.

**Organization**

* Lead and develop a global organization (30+).
* Grow and retain senior technical talent, and manage the pipeline, hiring, succession and career paths for architects and quality engineers.
* Build a collaborative partnership with Firmware, Hardware, Systems, Product and Program Management, and with the Optics and telemetry teams.
* Own the function's budget, headcount plan, requisitions and tooling or lab investments.

**Your Team**

You will lead a small team of senior leaders and architects who together cover the function end to end, with architecture and quality responsibilities intentionally overlapping:

* Software quality assurance and release qualification.
* Hardware and firmware interlink.
* Optics and module architecture.
* Product and systems architecture.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Set a multi-year architecture and quality roadmap aligned with product and customer priorities, and drive it across engineering teams that do not report to you.
* Make and communicate hard trade-offs between schedule, scope and quality, and own the release recommendation.
* Raise the architecture bar: consistent patterns, reuse across product lines, and early detection of design risk before it becomes schedule risk.
* Shift quality left: embed test, automation and requirements quality earlier in the lifecycle, and invest in CI/CD, simulation, emulation and lab infrastructure.
* Represent Architecture & Quality in executive reviews and in technical engagements with key customers and standards bodies.
* Keep the function independent and credible: escalate quality risks directly and transparently, including when the news is unwelcome.
* Build the next layer of leadership so the function does not depend on any one person, and set clear delegation across the architecture and SQA leads.
* Manage a distributed team across time zones with clear rituals, ownership and handoffs.

**What We're Looking For**

* BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
* 15+ years in embedded firmware or systems software for semiconductor, networking or optical products, including 8+ years leading managers or senior technical leaders.
* Track record owning both architecture and quality outcomes for shipping firmware products at scale.
* Deep working knowledge of firmware architecture for connectivity or optics products, with direct experience in HW/FW co-design and silicon bring-up.
* Hands-on experience with test strategy and automation, release qualification and quality metrics for complex, customer-deployed products.
* Experience leading globally distributed teams across multiple sites and cultures, including offshore QA/SQA organizations.
* Proven executive communication: able to present risk, trade-offs and recommendations to VP-level and customer audiences.

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience with CMIS and optical module firmware (for example 400G/800G and coherent or pluggable optics), and related industry standards and interoperability programs.
* Familiarity with Ethernet PHY, retimer, DSP or SerDes firmware, and with security features such as MACsec.
* Experience with secure firmware update, recovery and lifecycle practices.
* Background building or transforming an SQA organization, including automation and CI/CD maturity.
* Experience in a matrixed, platform-style organization where architecture is a shared service.

**Expected Base Pay Range (USD)**

218,850 - 327,800, $ per annum

The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.

**Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements**

Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights include an employee stock purchase plan with a 2-year look back, family support programs to help balance work and home life, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and a recognition and service awards to celebrate contributions and milestones. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

**Interview Integrity**

To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process.

**This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment.**
